anti_overlap: Does NOT cover Claude Code hooks (fd-claude-code-hooks-economy)
Does NOT cover prompt cache shape (fd-prompt-cache-economics)
decision_lens: Is this MCP server pulling its weight per session — does it provide value commensurate with its instructions text, deferred-tool listing, and startup latency?
focus: Reviews MCP server inventory for startup cost, deferred-tool bloat, and instructions injected per session
name: fd-mcp-server-hygiene
persona: Apply the perspective of an MCP server operator — they care about each server's startup latency, the size of its tool catalog, the cost of its `instructions` block in the host's system prompt, and how many tools sit deferred but listed
review_areas: Deferred tool listing cost: ~80 tool names listed at session start — what is the byte/token cost, and how often are they actually used per session (cass analytics tools)?
MCP `instructions` blocks: which servers inject the longest instruction text, and is the instruction load-bearing or aspirational marketing?
Tool-name length: do MCP tool names use unnecessarily long prefixes (`mcp__plugin_interflux_openrouter-dispatch__review_with_model`) — could the registry collapse the namespace?
MCP startup latency: which servers add startup time but rarely provide tools used in-session?
Tool schema fetch: ToolSearch loads schemas on-demand. Are there servers whose tools should be schema-deferred entirely until first use?
Disconnection handling: when an MCP server disconnects (context7, exa, interrank, intersearch — all disconnected this session), is the tool list cleanly reaped or does it leak

severity_examples.condition: The instructions cost more than the tools save
severity_examples.scenario: An MCP server injects 500+ tokens of instructions every session but its tools are used in <5% of sessions (per cass analytics tools)

severity_examples.condition: Tool listing alone consumes 5kt across the deferred-tool section
severity_examples.scenario: An MCP tool name is 70+ characters long because of nested namespace prefixes

severity_examples.condition: Stale tool listings consume tokens for tools that cannot be invoked
severity_examples.scenario: A disconnected MCP server's tools remain listed as deferred in subsequent turns until session restart

source_domain: MCP server lifecycle and Claude Code agent SDK
success_hints: Count actual tool usage per server using cass analytics tools
Quote specific instructions blocks and propose compressed versions
Recommend servers for full removal, lazy-load, or instructions-trim
Reference the disconnected-server pattern visible in this session
task_context: Sylveste loads ~80 deferred MCP tools at session start (visible in deferred-tools listing). Each MCP server can inject `instructions` text into the system prompt. Some servers (interlock, interlab, interlens, interflux exa, context7) inject substantial instructions and large tool lists. Identify which servers are not justifying their per-session cost and propose lazy-load or removal.
